source.title: From Growing to Looping: A Unified View of Iterative Computation in LLMs
source.authors: Ferdinand Kapl; Emmanouil Angelis; Kaitlin Maile; Johannes von Oswald; Stefan Bauer

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether changing model depth and weight sharing at matched unique-parameter counts changes held-out NLL; it does not fit or test scaling laws.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports held-out NLL for standard and looped model configurations. These matched-parameter comparisons bear on V4. The paper does not fit power laws, make small-run extrapolations, find compute-optimal allocations, or test the other claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version of the claim. It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only to motivate the work. Its NLL comparisons set looped models against standard models with the same unique-layer count. The looped models run 2 to 8 times more effective depth, so per-token compute differs. That is not V4's fixed-parameter shape comparison, where depth versus width varies at roughly constant compute per parameter. No power laws are fitted, no extrapolation is made, and no compute-optimal split or loss-to-downstream predictability is tested. The depth-grown models have the same final architecture as the baseline; only the training procedure differs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that looped and depth-grown models share depth-wise signatures of iterative computation and are composable ('grow first, loop later' gives the best reasoning). They report that depth-grown models match baseline NLL and broad benchmarks with about 80% of training compute while improving reasoning. They draw no conclusions about scaling laws.
record.recipe_differences: Compares standard, looped, and depth-grown transformer configurations and measures held-out NLL; does not perform a scaling-law fit or compute-optimal allocation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Held-out NLL varies with the loop configuration and matched standard reference; the tested configurations include different unique-layer counts and recurrence layouts.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed unique-parameter count, looping a block to increase effective depth lowers held-out NLL by 0.04 to 0.17 at the 360M configuration. At the 1.7B configuration it lowers NLL with few unique layers (2.29→2.12) but raises it with 12 unique layers (2.01→2.07, 2.05). Iso-inference looped models stay above the full baseline NLL.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss of weight-shared (looped) transformers depends on both unique parameters and effective depth/compute; extra recurrence helps most when unique parameters are few.

record.problems: The architecture comparison covers a limited set of configurations. Uncertainty estimates are not stated for the Table 1 NLL values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant rows left out. Depth-grown models have the same final depth as the baseline; their different training procedure is not a separate test of architecture shape for V4.

untested.parts: No depth/width/aspect-ratio variation at fixed parameter count and compute; width is held fixed.
No other modalities or regimes are fitted with power laws.
Downstream scores are reported but not related to scale or loss as a predictive trend.

record.verdict_notes: The record's size labels are swapped. Table 1's 32-layer block (baseline NLL 2.18) is SmolLM-360M and the 24-layer block (NLL 1.96) is 1.7B, per Section 3.2's text and Section 4. The reader's V4 'supports' label is dropped because the looped-versus-standard comparisons change compute per token, not shape at fixed N.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fits of held-out loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No extrapolation from small runs to larger runs.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation sweep or fitted growth trends.
Tests a limited set of depth and weight-sharing configurations at matched unique-parameter counts; does not vary width or establish behavior across a wide range of architectures.
No other modalities or training regimes of the kinds named in this version are tested for power-law loss.
Reports downstream benchmark results, but does not test their predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
No scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal splits are fitted or compared across fitting choices.

rows.subject: Loop (4×8)
rows.operation_detail: Compared held-out NLL with a standard model at the same unique-layer count.
rows.note: Matched-parameter comparison; the NLL difference is 0.17.
rows.check: Iso-param comparison of Loop (4×8) with Standard 4/4. The looped model has 8× the effective depth and inference FLOPs, so this is a weight-sharing/compute effect, not a shape change at fixed N. Size is wrong: 32-layer models are the 360M configuration, not 1.7B. The text pairs Loop (16×2) with 360M and Loop (12×2) with 1.7B, and SmolLM-360M has 32 layers.
